text.label: Demo review: “Tallyo” is a fictional invoicing app; screenshots and measurements are real, taken from the demo pages in evals/fixtures/demo-site
text.headline: Keyboard focus is invisible on [[all 32]] controls, and the phone page scrolls sideways
text.lead: The landing page looks tidy at 1280 px but breaks down at the edges: focus rings are removed, grey text fails contrast, a late promo bar shifts the page, and below 1280 the feature strip pushes the page to 1,096 px wide. Most fixes are one-line CSS changes.
text.checksNote: Measured with inspect_ui.py at 1280×800, 768×1024 and 360×780 on home, and at 1280 on pricing. Focus was checked by tabbing through both pages at 1280. The tick marks the target.
text.lensesH: Colour, responsive behaviour and spacing are the weakest lenses
text.lensesP: A score of 0–100 shows how well the interface handles each lens on the screens checked. Below 40 means big problems. There is no dark mode (no prefers-color-scheme rules); that lens is scored on the light theme alone.
text.shotsP: Each numbered box is an issue from the table; click its number to jump to the plan. Red boxes are critical or in the top 3.
text.screensH: The page holds at 1280 and comes apart at 768 and 360
text.screensP: The home page at three widths, then pricing.
text.matrixH: {qw} quick wins with high impact and low effort
text.matrixP: Each dot is an issue. Black dots fix the current UI; outlined red dots are rethinks to test first.
text.opsP: ICE = impact × confidence × ease (each 1–10). Severity (1–4) says how bad; ICE says what to do first.
text.nextP: Each has a hypothesis, a success metric and the cheapest way to check it.
text.planH: Full plan: all {n} fixes with selectors, widths and target values
text.planP: For every issue: why it is here, where (page, width, selector, screenshot mark), current and target values, steps, metric, effort and risk. The top three also list alternatives, an experiment with a threshold and a pre-mortem.
text.dataH: Confidence is fairly high: every value was measured, but there is no behaviour data
text.dataP: Out of scope and left to ux-review: the sign-up fields use placeholders instead of labels, the password field is type=text, and the button says “Submit”. The pricing countdown that restarts on every load is a trust issue for ux-review and product-lens-audit, not a UI one.
how: Checked sources: a shell with Playwright that reaches the pages; questions skipped, assumptions noted.

Ran inspect_ui.py on home at 1280, 768 and 360 and on pricing at 1280: screenshots, element boxes, computed styles, contrast, scale, tap targets, dark-mode and reduced-motion emulation, CLS, and a Tab walk for focus.
Went through the 13 UI lenses; every finding is labelled observed or hypothesis and cites a WCAG criterion where one applies.
Scored severity and ICE, compared alternatives for the top three, ran a pre-mortem, built both outputs, render-checked the report and traced every number back to the inspect output.
text.footer: demo data: fictional product, real measurements of the demo pages

kpis.l: keyboard stops with a visible focus

maturity.note: Usable at 1280 for a mouse user. Not yet Consistent: four button shapes, eleven font sizes, eleven off-scale spacing values, and the layout breaks at 768 and 360.

screens.p: Two CTAs compete; grey text fails
Sideways scroll; promo shifts the page

ops.t: Bring back the keyboard focus ring (0 of 32 stops show focus)
Raise grey text to AA: 16 of 39 text elements fail at 1280
One primary action: the pulsing orange “Book a demo” outweighs “Get started free”
Stop the sideways scroll below 1280: the feature strip makes the page 1,096–1,117 px wide
Reserve space for the promo bar: it lands at ≈ 750 ms and shifts the page (CLS 0.137 at 360)
Respect reduced motion: the demo button pulses forever, even with reduce set
Use one icon style: outline, filled and emoji icons sit side by side
Cut the type scale from 11 sizes to 6 and lift text under 12 px
Put spacing on a 4 px scale (11 of 18 values are off it)
One button shape instead of four radii (4, 6, 12, 999 px)
Bring the oranges back into the palette (#e8572a, #d2471d are not brand colours)
Give 768 px its own layout: the hero keeps two columns and the H1 runs to 4 lines
Enlarge phone tap targets: 9 of 17 are under 24 px, the menu button is 32 px
Show a 2-line max on the hero subtitle at 360 (5 lines now)
Decide on dark mode: none today, light colours are hard-coded
Test a single-column hero: one CTA, sign-up card below

1.h: If focus is visible again, keyboard users can see where they are and finish sign-up, because every control shows a ring when tabbed to.
1.m: Keyboard stops with a visible focus: 32 of 32 (now 0)
1.t: Delete one CSS rule, add :focus-visible, rerun inspect_ui.py (≈15 min)

2.h: If secondary text uses #6b7280 instead of the three pale greys, the subtitle and small print become readable for low-vision visitors and in sunlight.
2.t: Swap the greys in style.css and rerun inspect_ui.py at 3 widths

4.h: If the strip wraps instead of overflowing, phones and tablets stop scrolling sideways and the browser stops zooming the page out.
4.m: Page width equals viewport at 360 and 768
4.t: Add flex-wrap to .strip and rerun inspect_ui.py at 360/768

1.why: style.css has *:focus { outline: none } and nothing in its place. A Tab walk at 1280 found 0 of 23 stops on home and 0 of 9 on pricing with any visible change (WCAG 2.4.7). Keyboard users cannot see where they are.
steps: Delete *:focus { outline: none }.
Add :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary); outline-offset: 2px }.
Rerun inspect_ui.py: focus visible must be 23 of 23 and 9 of 9.
1.metric: Keyboard stops with a visible focus: 32 of 32 (now 0)
1.risk: Mouse users see no ring with :focus-visible, so their view does not change.
alt: Box-shadow ring: also valid; outline chosen because it survives Windows high-contrast mode.
Underline links on focus only: not enough for buttons and inputs.
1.pm: It shipped and focus was still invisible on the blue Submit button, because the ring was the same blue. Use outline-offset so the ring sits on the white around it.

2.why: 16 of 39 text elements at 1280 fail WCAG AA (1.4.3): the hero subtitle #a3a9b4 on white = 2.36:1, “No card needed” and the feature strip #8d94a1 = 3.05:1, the Terms links #a3a9b4 on #f6f7fb = 2.21:1, footer links 2.36:1. On pricing “/mo per seat” is 2.36:1 and the VAT note #b8bec9 is 1.87:1.
steps: Add --color-text-muted: #6b7280.
Replace #a3a9b4, #8d94a1 and #b8bec9 for text with it; keep pale greys for borders only.
Rerun inspect_ui.py at 3 widths; only the demo button (#3) may still fail.
2.risk: Heavier look; keep hierarchy with size and weight, not paler grey.
alt: Darken only the subtitle: leaves 15 failures.
A darker #5d6472 (5.95:1): kept in reserve for new surfaces.
2.thr: 0 text elements below AA on the 4 screenshots
2.pm: The check still failed because greys were hard-coded in six places and two were missed. Search style.css for every hex value first.

3.why: Two filled buttons of the same size sit side by side - “Get started free” (#3156d3, 180×46) and “Book a demo” (#e8572a, 153×46) - and the sign-up card adds a third filled “Submit”. The orange one wins the eye: it is the only warm colour on the page and it pulses (#6). Its white text is 3.6:1. At 360 the two stack and the form drops below the fold.
steps: Make “Book a demo” a secondary outline button.
Keep “Get started free” as the only filled button in the hero.
5-second test with 5 people: what would you click first?
3.metric: First clicks on the primary action (5-second / first-click test)
3.risk: Demo requests may drop; watch them for 2 weeks.

4.why: The feature strip is five 200 px items in a non-wrapping flex row with overflow: visible. At 768 the page becomes 1,117 px wide and at 360 1,096 px; the browser offers sideways scroll and phones may zoom the page out (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow).

change.cur: no wrap; span width 200px, flex none
change.tgt: flex-wrap: wrap; gap 8px 16px; span width auto

steps: Set .strip { flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px 16px } and drop the fixed width on .strip span.
Rerun inspect_ui.py at 360, 768 and 1280: no SIDEWAYS SCROLL line.
4.metric: Page width equals viewport at 360 and 768
4.risk: The strip becomes 2–3 lines on phones.
alt: Hide the strip below 768: loses content.
Horizontal scroller with snap: fine, but a hidden overflow on a key selling point.
4.pm: The strip was fixed but the 5-item nav overflowed at 768 next. Rerun the check at every width, not only the one in the ticket.

5.why: A promo bar (“New: recurring invoices for retainers”) is inserted by script ≈ 750 ms after load at the top of the page, 88 px tall (107 px at 360). Everything below jumps down: CLS 0.068 at 1280, 0.085 at 768 and 0.137 at 360 (above the 0.1 limit). The shifted nodes are main, header.top and the sign-up button.

change.tgt: rendered in the HTML, or a reserved 88px slot (min-height) from first paint

steps: Render the promo in the HTML, or reserve its height with a placeholder of the same size.
Rerun inspect_ui.py: CLS ≤ 0.1 at all widths.

6.why: “Book a demo” runs an infinite 1.6 s box-shadow pulse. There are no prefers-reduced-motion rules, and with reduce emulated the animation still runs (1 running animation).

change.tgt: none, or 2 iterations and none under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce

steps: Remove the infinite pulse, or limit it to 2 runs.
Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation: none !important; transition: none !important } } as a safety net.

7.why: The three feature icons mix styles: an outline clock (1.6 stroke), a filled bell and a 📋 emoji. The feature strip uses ★ characters and pricing a 🔥 emoji. Four icon languages on two pages.
steps: Pick one outline icon set (the clock already matches).
Replace the bell, the emoji and the ★ characters with icons from that set.

8.why: Eleven distinct font sizes on home (10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 20, 22, 28, 46 px), with 13 and 14 px used side by side for similar text. 8 text elements per width are under 12 px (social labels 10 px, footer links 11 px); body text is 14 px with line-height 1.3.
steps: Define 6 size tokens and map every font-size to the nearest.
Set body to 16px/1.5.
8.metric: Distinct font sizes ≤ 6; text under 12 px: 0

9.why: Paddings, margins and gaps take 18 distinct values; 11 are off a 4 px scale: 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 14, 18, 22, 26, 34, 37 px (e.g. header 13px 37px, card 26px 22px, strip 18px 37px).
steps: Add spacing tokens.
Replace off-scale values; one page padding (40px at 1280, 16px at 360).

10.why: Buttons use four corner radii: 12 px (Get started), 999 px (Book a demo), 4 px (Submit, Log in) and 6 px (pricing Choose). Four shapes read as four components.
steps: Add radius.md (8px) and use it on every button.
Remove per-button overrides.

11.why: The brand palette is blue (#3156d3) and navy (#1d2433), yet two unrelated oranges appear: the demo button #e8572a and the pricing countdown #d2471d on #fff1ec (4.09:1). Five greys are used for text.

change.tgt: brand blue for actions; one warning colour token if needed

steps: Replace the oranges with brand colours (see #3).
Merge the text greys into two tokens (see #2).

12.why: At 768 the hero keeps the desktop two-column layout (the breakpoint is 700 px): the 46 px H1 wraps to 4 lines in a 352 px column (199 px tall) while the card sits beside it. The nav shows all 5 items.
steps: Move the single-column breakpoint to 1024 px, or scale the H1 with clamp(32px, 5vw, 46px).
Check 768 and 820.

13.why: At 360, 9 of 17 tap targets are under 24 px (WCAG 2.5.8): four social links 18×18 and five footer links 14 px high. The menu button is 32×32; only 2 of 17 reach 44×44.
steps: Make .social a and .burger 44×44 with the icon centred.
Pad footer links to 24 px tall.

14.why: At 360 the hero subtitle runs 5 lines (123 px) in pale grey between the H1 and the buttons, pushing the primary button to 60% of the screen.
steps: Shorten the subtitle on small screens or drop it to 15 px.
Check the primary button lands in the top half at 360.
14.metric: Primary button within the top 55% at 360
14.risk: Copy change: agree with whoever owns the text.

15.why: No prefers-color-scheme rules and no color-scheme meta: the page is light only, with colours hard-coded. Nothing breaks; whether users want a dark landing page is unknown.
steps: Move colours to tokens first (#2, #11).
Decide with product whether a dark theme is worth it for an app the landing leads into.

16.why: The hero offers three ways in (two buttons and a form). A single-column hero with one CTA and the sign-up card below might lift starts; there is no behaviour data, so this is a hypothesis.
steps: Add click tracking on the three entry points.
Run an A/B test for 2 weeks: current vs single-column hero.
16.risk: Card below the fold may lose sign-ups from returning visitors.

answers.a: Skipped. Assumption: phone and desktop equally; no dark mode
Skipped. Assumption: infer tokens from CSS; brand blue #3156d3

WCAG.d: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. Level AA is the usual legal target. Numbers like 1.4.3 are its success criteria.

AA.d: Contrast: normal text 4.5:1, large text 3:1, icons and focus rings 3:1. #a3a9b4 on white is 2.36:1.

CTA.d: The primary button; here “Get started free”.

CLS.d: How much visible content jumps while loading. ≤ 0.1 is good; the demo reaches 0.137 at 360.

Tap targets.d: WCAG 2.5.8 asks ≥ 24×24 px; 44×44 px is comfortable.

focus.d: The element that receives keys; a visible ring shows keyboard users where they are (WCAG 2.4.7).

token.d: A named colour, size or spacing (color.text-muted = #6b7280) instead of a hard-coded value.

tokens.d: Named colours, sizes and spacing used instead of hard-coded values.

inspect_ui.py.d: Part of this skill: screenshots at 3 widths, computed styles, contrast, scale, tap targets, dark and reduced-motion emulation, CLS and a focus walk.

5-second test.d: Show the screen for 5 seconds and ask what it was about and what to click.

pre-mortem.d: Imagine the fix shipped and nothing improved, then explain why.

A/B test.d: Half the visitors see the new version, half the old.

Reflow.d: WCAG 1.4.10: content fits a 320 px wide viewport without scrolling in two directions.
